layout_thesis.statement: A coop-shelf editorial: every section reads like a slat on a tasting counter under warm yellow light, with the bottle lineup treated as the shelf, the founders as the chalkboard above, and recipes as small hand-written cards pinned between. The page earns the word 'real' by showing it — ingredient flat-lays, bottle drop-shadows, finished drinks — rather than centering a slogan over a stock sunset.
layout_thesis.audience: Home drinkers shopping DTC, mixed with the bartender curious about a small Charleston label; secondarily the trade buyer checking the line at a glance.
layout_thesis.job_to_be_done: Convince a shopper in under 30 seconds that these mixers are made by real bartenders with real ingredients, and let them pick a bottle or pick a recipe without a tour of pages.
layout_thesis.why_this_not_generic: Most cocktail-mixer brand sites open with a saturated bottle dead-center on a sunset gradient, then a 3-up feature grid (real / natural / easy). We refuse both. The shelf runs the page vertically, the yellow is the page color (not a hero band), and the founder chalkboard replaces the feature grid. Type pairing is Fraunces over Inter (not Inter-everywhere), with the wordmark's tail letters rendered in a contrast weight as the recurring signature.

sections.purpose: Set the wordmark and the page temperature (yellow field, Charleston dateline). It is not a hero with a CTA — it is a tasting-room header that shows where you are before you scroll.
sections.component: Wordmark + dateline strip across a #FFC517 band, with a thin #CDBD81 rule under it; wordmark spelled out 'Barcoop Bevy' with 'vy' set in the contrasting tail weight as the recurring signature.
sections.rationale: The live site's wordmark IS the logo. We honor that by letting the wordmark carry the masthead instead of inventing a separate glyph. The chicken-coop yellow is the page background, not an accent band.

sections.purpose: Show all seven 1L bottles together on one shelf so the shopper can read the line at a glance — the way a bartender sees a back-bar. Each bottle is clickable, no copy walls, no carousel.
sections.component: Vertical shelf: seven PNG bottle drop-shadows in a single horizontal row on a #FFF7C5 counter. Bottle name and single-line descriptor sit on a chalkboard card laid flat under each bottle (no icon, no price badge).
sections.rationale: Bottles are the brand's most powerful owned asset. Showing all seven together (instead of a single feature bottle) is the structural alternative to the 'single hero bottle' pattern. The shelf itself becomes the navigation.

media.alt: Classic Margarita 1L bottle on its drop-shadow, center of a seven-bottle lineup
media.rationale: Use the Classic Margarita as the visual anchor of the row because it is the brand's flagship; remaining bottles sit to either side at the same scale.

sections.purpose: Replace the founders' bio with a chalkboard strip: who made it, where, and the single hardest sentence about ingredients. This is the trust section, written like a chalkboard above a bar pass.
sections.component: Two-column: left half is a portrait of the founders (square crop, no overlay), right half is Fraunces-set copy on a chalkboard black (#3D3D3D) panel with a single thin yellow rule. No 'meet the team' icon, no timeline.
sections.rationale: Founders photo is brand-owned and alt-tagged with their names. Putting their faces next to the chalkboard statement answers 'made by real people' before the shopper has to ask.

media.alt: Joe and MariElena Raya, founders of Barcoop Bevy
media.rationale: Square crop suits a side-by-side with the chalkboard panel and avoids any tilt-shift or gallery treatment.

sections.purpose: Show the actual ingredients in one flat-lay so the word 'real' stops being a claim and becomes a photo. Below it, the four ingredient rules the brand repeats (no HFCS, no preservatives, no artificial anything) sit as four rule-lines, not as four icon cards.
sections.component: Full-bleed ingredient flat-lay on the #FBF7E9 cream body. Under it, four typographic rules stacked vertically with thin #CDBD81 dividers — copy only, no icons, no rounded badges.
sections.rationale: This is the single section where the banned 'artisanal / craft' language gets replaced by plain English. Flat-lay is the brand's own shot, not stock.

media.alt: Flat-lay of real cocktail ingredients — citrus, cucumbers, strawberries, herbs, chilies, sea salt
media.rationale: Full-bleed gives the flat-lay room to be read like a market photo; this is the single most 'real' image the brand owns.

sections.purpose: Teach the 2:1 mixing rule (and the 4:1 Bloody Mary rule) without writing a tutorial page. This is the brand's most repeated sentence across all product pages; it deserves a section of its own.
sections.component: Oversized Fraunces numerals in the page yellow — '2 : 1' rendered as a typographic poster, with the Bloody Mary '4 : 1' set smaller beneath. No bottle, no illustration.
sections.rationale: Branding a numeric ratio in type is the structural alternative to the 'three easy steps' infographic. This is one rule the brand owns.

sections.purpose: Feature the award-winning Bloody Mary alone — but on a flat counter (a regular surface, not a pedestal), so it reads as one bottle you can reach for, not a luxury product.
sections.component: Single oversized bottle render left, copy right. Bottle stands on the same #FFF7C5 cream counter the lineup sits on. Press hit (SOFI Gold 2024) sits as a small caption line below the product name.
sections.rationale: Awards are press hits, not testimonials — they earn a caption, not a banner. One bottle + one paragraph is the right scale for this brand.

media.alt: Bloody Mary 1L bottle on its drop-shadow, the brand's flagship award-winner
media.rationale: Inset leaves room for the award caption and ingredient origin note without crowding the bottle.

sections.purpose: Six recipe cards pinned between the bottle section and the press section, written in the brand's short lines ('light and bright with a hint of vacation in your glass'). Mix of cocktail and mocktail to surface the NA story without naming it.
sections.component: A 2x3 asymmetric grid of square drink photos. Each card has the drink name in Fraunces, the mixer + spirit in the muted brown #765F2C, no body copy, no badges.
sections.rationale: Six cards (four cocktails + two NA) is enough to show range without becoming a recipe library. Cards beat a carousel because every drink is photographable.

media.alt: Skinny Margarita finished drink in a rocks glass with salted rim
media.rationale: Skinny Margarita anchors the grid because it bridges cocktail and NA (also used as Lite Limeade mocktail elsewhere) and gives the strongest yellow tone against the cream page.

sections.purpose: Surface the NA / mocktail story in two photo cards so the brand doesn't have to invent a whole NA line — the mixers themselves do the work, paired with soda water or just ice.
sections.component: Two square NA drink photos in a tight 1x2 strip on the cream body, with one typographic line per card reading 'just ice' or 'just soda water'.
sections.rationale: NA is half the use-case across the recipes; giving it a section is the alternative to burying it under 'mix with any spirit' copy.

media.alt: Virgin Piña Colada mocktail with toasted coconut garnish
media.rationale: Piña Colada in NA form is the brand's most 'vacation in your glass' image; pairing with the limeade gives one sweet, one tart.

sections.purpose: Show editor coverage as a single horizontal log line strip — Wirecutter, Boston Globe, Authority Magazine, SFA — not as press logos on cards.
sections.component: Single typographic strip on #FFF7C5 cream with four publication names set in Fraunces small caps separated by thin #CDBD81 pipes. No logos, no card backgrounds.
sections.rationale: Press coverage is verified (NY Times Wirecutter, Boston Globe, Authority Magazine, SFA), but there are no customer testimonials. A log line respects the honesty rule and keeps the visual quiet.

sections.purpose: Send the shopper to the cart with the lineup repeated at small scale so they can pick a bottle without scrolling back up. No 'subscribe and save' sidebar.
sections.component: A condensed repeat of the lineup strip rendered as clickable thumbnails (no full bottles) with the headline 'pick your bottle' and a single teal #259E7E 'shop the lineup' affordance.
sections.rationale: Shop CTA on a single bottle would default to 'single hero + buy now' — repeating the lineup makes the decision structural, not promotional.

media.alt: Classic Margarita 1L bottle thumbnail repeated with the rest of the lineup
media.rationale: Re-use the flagship bottle at thumbnail scale so the repeat-strip reads as the same lineup rather than a new image set.

sections.purpose: Quietly close with the four operator-facing touch points (wholesale, press, contact, FAQ at /about#faq) and the Charleston dateline. No newsletter signup, no stock-location widget.
sections.component: Single-row footer in #3D3D3D on the yellow field. Small Fraunces for the wordmark repeat, Inter for the four links separated by thin rules.
sections.rationale: FAQ lives at /about#faq, not /faq (the /faq route is a 404 — flagged in limitations). Footer keeps links truthful.

signature_element.name: The Coop Tail
signature_element.description: The last two letters of the wordmark ('vy') are set in a high-contrast Fraunces weight against the page's chicken-coop yellow — a single ligature that reads as a chicken's tail feather at full size. The same 'vy' is echoed as the URL slug, the social handle suffix, and as a repeated corner mark on the recipe cards.
signature_element.why_it_fits_brand: The wordmark IS the logo on the live site (no SVG/PNG asset exists). Honoring that by treating its last two letters as the brand's repeating motif — instead of inventing a chicken icon we cannot license — keeps the asset surface honest and gives the page a recognizable micro-detail without becoming an iconographic system.
signature_element.implementation_note: Render the wordmark with 'Barcoop Be' in Fraunces 500 / yellow field / dark text, then 'vy' in Fraunces 800 italic at ~1.4x size with the final descender clipped into the rule below. On cards, draw the same clipped descender as a 12px corner mark in #765F2C. No SVG chicken, no clip-art.

effects: wordmark 'vy' tail nudges 4px left on hover, no other motion on the masthead
shelf lineup bottles lift 8px on individual hover with a soft 250ms ease-out, no parallax, no shimmer
recipe cards fade-stagger 60ms on first viewport entry, no bouncing, no zoom
numeric ratio '2 : 1' does a single type-set swap to '4 : 1' on scroll into the Bloody Mary section
no scroll-jacking, no marquee, no video background
motion_vocabulary.rationale: The brand's voice is plain and low-jargon ('just add spirit', 'made by real people'); motion must match. Anything cinematic would over-perform the copy and slip toward the 'luxury / artisanal' feel the brand explicitly bans.

copy_blocks.text: Charleston, South Carolina — just add spirit.
Made by bartenders. Made in Charleston, South Carolina.
No artificial ingredients, preservatives or high fructose corn sugar. Only real ingredients made by real people in Charleston.
Real citrus. Real cucumber. Real strawberry. Real ginger. Real cane sugar. Real sea salt. Real peppers. Real herbs. Just real.
Two parts mixer. One part spirit. (Bloody Mary: four parts mixer, one part spirit.) Just add spirit.
Bloody Mary — Smoked Sea Salt + Chiles.
SOFI Gold 2024. Silver SIP 2023. SFA Product of the Year — Beverage 2024.
Just pour. Just stir. Just enjoy.
A perfect mix of bold and juicy flavors.
Skip the spirit. Keep the bev.
Soda water or just ice. Same bottle. Same real ingredients.
As featured in NY Times Wirecutter, Boston Globe, Authority Magazine, Specialty Food Association.
Wholesale · Press · Contact · FAQ — made in Charleston.

skipped_sections.reason: There are no customer testimonials on the live site; press coverage exists but is editor-led, not quote-led. Brand donts forbid inventing testimonials.
The brand's voice is conversational and B2C; no email capture exists on the live site and adding one would change the commercial surface.
No retail locator component exists on the live site; off-premise distribution is documented on /wholesale but is operator-facing, not consumer-facing.

The operator's design_brief described a Marbella, Spain wholesaler; the live site is a Charleston DTC mixer brand with a B2B tier that has no public pricing. The B2B surface cannot be designed without resolving the brief mismatch with the operator first.
Instagram handle (@barcoopbevy) is verified on the site but no posts were fetched; image_url is null and captions are null per the honesty rule.

decisions.decision: Treat the wordmark 'vy' tail as the signature element rather than introduce a separate chicken or coop icon.
alternatives_considered: A colored monogram on a circular badge
decisions.why_chosen: The live site has no separate logo asset — the wordmark IS the logo. Introducing a new icon would create an asset that does not exist in the brand's owned image set; reusing the wordmark's terminal letters keeps the signature inside verified evidence.

decisions.decision: Show all seven bottles together on one shelf rather than hero a single bottle.
alternatives_considered: Carousel with one bottle per slide
Three featured bottles in a row
decisions.why_chosen: Seven bottles is the actual product range. A carousel hides five products; a single hero compresses the brand to one SKU. The shelf-as-navigation is the structural alternative to the standard DTC hero.

decisions.decision: Use Fraunces over Inter everywhere for headings, with Inter only at body sizes.
alternatives_considered: Recoleta paid Klim face as briefed
A slab serif like Roboto Slab
decisions.why_chosen: Recoleta is paid and cannot be vendored; Fraunces (OFL) is the briefed substitute. All-Inter is explicitly the aesthetic the brand is NOT. A slab serif would push toward the banned 'artisanal' territory.

decisions.decision: Pair the founder portrait with a chalkboard typography panel rather than 'meet the team' icon cards.
alternatives_considered: Three-up team grid with role icons
decisions.why_chosen: The brand owns one founder portrait; inventing more would breach the brand's owned asset list. A chalkboard aligns with the 'made by bartenders' line and keeps the section to one photograph plus one paragraph.

decisions.decision: Surface the 2:1 ratio as a typographic poster rather than a 'how to use' three-step block.
alternatives_considered: Video loop of a bartender shaking
decisions.why_chosen: The brand repeats 'just add spirit' across every product page; the ratio IS the instruction. One oversized numeral teaches the standard faster than three paragraphs and stays on-brand.

alternatives_considered: Rewrite press hits as customer testimonials
decisions.why_chosen: Brand donts forbid inventing testimonials; press coverage cannot be paraphrased as quotes without misrepresenting the source. Empty is correct here.

decisions.decision: Leave the FAQ at /about#faq and do not link to /faq in the footer.
alternatives_considered: Inline the FAQs as an accordion
decisions.why_chosen: The /faq route returns a 404. Linking to it would ship a broken footer. The /about#faq anchor is the verified working path per the brief's limitations.
